headline: Use {arm:brisk-s.few}: it is the only configuration of {n_candidates|int} that clears every gate, by {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.gap|abs|pts} points at its narrowest, on overall accuracy.
lede: Every configuration more accurate than it misses the p95 latency budget, and the far cheaper {arm:nano-xs.few} misses the Complex × News floor clearly. The narrow overall clearance is still wider than the noise the cell intervals imply, so what would change the call is a fresh sample that fails to reproduce it.
flag: Balanced accuracy, the overall gate's measure, has no stated interval; the cell accuracies it averages do, and they put the overall clearance outside the noise.

caveats.material_if: only if the cell intervals understate the uncertainty, for example if turns cluster by conversation: balanced accuracy is the plain mean of disjoint cells, each known to within {cells.complex.conv.brisk-s.few.accuracy.half_width|abs|pts} points for {arm:brisk-s.few}, so its own interval is far narrower than the clearance, but no tool states it

only if the gold labels are noisy for medium complexity or Complex × News, where the errors and the binding cell sit: label noise shifts the readings against the absolute gates and can reorder close configurations

decision.text: Serve the turn router on {arm:brisk-s.few}. It clears every gate, at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.few} a month at current volume.

{arm:nano-xs.few} costs {cost_per_month.nano-xs.few} a month and is nearly as accurate on the production traffic mix, but its Complex × News accuracy, {criteria.cell_floor.nano-xs.few.complex.news.value}, sits below the floor by more than its interval ({cells.complex.news.nano-xs.few.accuracy.half_width|abs|pts} points).
{arm:brisk-s.rubric}, {arm:atlas-m.few} and {arm:atlas-m.rubric} are more accurate, but each misses the p95 budget of {criteria.p95.threshold}.
{arm:atlas-m.zero}, {arm:brisk-s.zero}, {arm:nano-xs.zero} and {arm:nano-xs.rubric} fall below the overall accuracy gate.

Overall accuracy is the narrowest clearance, {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.gap|abs|pts} points, and it belongs to the one configuration picked because it passed, which makes its estimate somewhat optimistic.

Complex × News is its weakest cell, {criteria.cell_floor.brisk-s.few.complex.news.gap|abs|pts} points above the floor and known to within {cells.complex.news.brisk-s.few.accuracy.half_width|abs|pts} points.
Confirm {arm:brisk-s.few} on a fresh sample of production turns: it settles whether the overall clearance survives outside the set it was picked on.

claims.text: {arm:brisk-s.few} is the only one of {n_candidates|int} model and prompt configurations that passes every gate.

evidence.caption: Each tile: balanced accuracy, cost, p95 latency and gate status, by model and prompt style.

claims.text: {arm:brisk-s.few} clears the overall accuracy gate by {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.gap|abs|pts} points, its narrowest clearance, yet wider than the noise: balanced accuracy averages disjoint cells, each known to within {cells.complex.conv.brisk-s.few.accuracy.half_width|abs|pts} points.

evidence.caption: Balanced accuracy per configuration against the overall gate; the snapshot states no interval for it, so the dots are bare.

claims.text: Complex × News is the weakest cell for every configuration, and it decides between the few-shot options of Brisk-S and Nano-XS: {arm:nano-xs.few} falls short of the floor at {criteria.cell_floor.nano-xs.few.complex.news.value}, while {arm:brisk-s.few} clears it by {criteria.cell_floor.brisk-s.few.complex.news.gap|abs|pts} points, each well beyond its interval.

evidence.caption: Accuracy in each cell for Brisk-S and Nano-XS few-shot, with case counts; the cells' intervals are not drawn by this block.
The same cells for every configuration, one panel each; Complex × News is the lowest cell in every panel.

claims.text: Every configuration more accurate than {arm:brisk-s.few} misses the p95 latency budget.

evidence.caption: Balanced accuracy against p95 latency on a log axis, with the overall gate and the latency budget; Nano-XS few-shot sits inside both but fails a cell floor, which this chart does not draw.

claims.text: Moving from few-shot to rubric + reasoning lifts Atlas-M and Brisk-S but drops Nano-XS to {measure.balanced_accuracy.nano-xs.rubric.mean}, by a similar amount in every cell, so the rubric's effect depends on the model.

evidence.caption: Balanced accuracy by model, one bar per prompt style, drawn from zero with the overall gate; few-shot beats zero-shot on every model, and only Nano-XS falls from few-shot to rubric + reasoning.
Nano-XS rubric + reasoning less Nano-XS few-shot, in points, per cell; the loss is spread across every cell rather than one complexity level.

explore.outcome: The call holds at any gate up to {criteria.overall.brisk-s.few.value}; above it, nothing passes.

explore.binds: every configuration's accuracy in each cell
explore.outcome: Below {criteria.cell_floor.nano-xs.few.complex.news.value} the call moves to {arm:nano-xs.few}; above {criteria.cell_floor.brisk-s.few.complex.news.value}, nothing passes.

Below {criteria.p95.brisk-s.few.value} nothing passes. At {criteria.p95.atlas-m.few.value} {arm:atlas-m.few} enters, {price.brisk-s.few.atlas-m.few.balanced_accuracy.gain|pts} points for {price.brisk-s.few.atlas-m.few.balanced_accuracy.monthly_cost_gap} more a month; at {criteria.p95.brisk-s.rubric.value} {arm:brisk-s.rubric} also enters, {price.brisk-s.few.brisk-s.rubric.balanced_accuracy.gain|pts} points for {price.brisk-s.few.brisk-s.rubric.balanced_accuracy.monthly_cost_gap} more, the cheaper step up. The gates still pick {arm:brisk-s.few} on cost; whether a point is worth that is the owner's call.

omitted.why: Not gated, and they order the configurations near the decision the same way; on traffic-weighted accuracy {arm:nano-xs.few} is within a fraction of a point of {arm:brisk-s.few}, which the why-not says.

Confusion over all turns can't show which axis fails inside Complex × News: both axes' diagonals for {arm:nano-xs.few} sit far above that cell's accuracy, and the per-axis tables don't reconcile with the cell accuracies until the definition of a correct turn is settled (a next step).
Its errors are medium complexity read as a neighbour, symmetric on both sides; it describes the error shape and doesn't change the call.
None lost or failed in any configuration; it describes the method.
The snapshot holds only p95 per configuration, so a p50-to-p95 range chart can't be drawn; p95 is what the gate reads.

omitted.what: A cascade that sends turns Nano-XS labels Complex × News on to Brisk-S
omitted.why: Nobody ran it, so no figure states its cost, accuracy or latency; and Complex × News is too large a share of turns for a second call to stay out of the p95 tail, so it would probably miss the latency budget (modelled, not measured).

next.text: Confirm {arm:brisk-s.few} on a fresh sample of production turns.
next.settles: Whether the overall clearance survives outside the set it was picked on; a shortfall there, not more cases on this set, is what could reverse the call.

next.text: Add Complex × News examples to Nano-XS's few-shot prompt and re-run that configuration.
next.settles: Whether the cheapest near-passing option can clear the cell floor; it costs {cost_per_month.nano-xs.few} a month against {cost_per_month.brisk-s.few}, but its own overall clearance, {criteria.overall.nano-xs.few.gap|abs|pts} points, is inside the noise the cell intervals imply, so it would need to gain overall too.

next.text: Declare whether a correct turn must match on both label axes, and break Complex × News errors down by axis.
next.settles: Which axis the binding cell fails on, and so which examples the Nano-XS fix should add.

next.text: Run Brisk-S with the rubric but without the reasoning step.
next.settles: Whether the rubric's accuracy gain over few-shot fits inside the latency budget; today the rubric and the reasoning step change together, so neither can be credited.

next.text: Double-label a sample of medium-complexity and Complex × News turns.
next.settles: How much of the remaining error, and of the narrow clearances, is label noise.

method.text: {scoreboard.brisk-s.few.cases|int} turns per configuration, the same turns for all {n_candidates|int}, spread over every complexity × domain cell; Complex × News holds {cells.complex.news.n_cases|int}. No repeats are recorded.
Each model crossed with each prompt style: zero-shot, few-shot examples, and a rubric with a reasoning step. There is no control; all {n_candidates|int} are new.

The share of turns whose predicted class matches the gold label. Balanced accuracy is the plain mean of the cell accuracies; traffic-weighted accuracy weights the cells by traffic. The snapshot does not say whether a turn must match on both axes, and its per-axis confusion tables don't reconcile with the cell accuracies.

Balanced accuracy at least {criteria.overall.threshold} overall; accuracy at least {criteria.cell_floor.threshold} in every cell; p95 latency at most {criteria.p95.threshold}. All were declared with the campaign; none was set after the results.
Cell accuracies carry intervals over turns. Balanced accuracy carries none; the page infers its width from the cell intervals, in words only. Latency and cost are single figures.
Gold class labels; no annotator agreement figure is recorded.
Cost per turn, at {meta.volume_per_month|int} turns a month.
